To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
odor always activates more glomeruli than one and that postsynaptic activation of glutamate receptors and calcium influx are major steps for the local CBF response to olfactory stimulation.

odor-evoked local CBF increases in the olfactory bulb are not triggered by postsynaptic calcium increases in single glomeruli but are rather a consequence of the activation of a large number of glomeruli.
odor-evoked CFF increases in the olfactory bulb are independent of postsynaptic responses, and that odor-evoked postsympatc calcium rises in mitral cells are required for the CFF increases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neurobiology of the olfactory system.
the mechanisms underlying neurovascular coupling in the olfactory bulb.
the mechanisms of neuronal activation and neurovascular coupling in the olfactory system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
odor-evoked Cerebral Blood Flow (CBF) increases are triggered by postsynaptic glutamatergic activity.
in the rodent glomerulus the postsynaptic activity, but not the presynaptic activity, is necessary for the local CBF increase.
the relationship between neuronal and vascular activity is not simple, but it is not as complex as previously suggested.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

in the olfactory glomerulus, the local increase in CBF depends on the activation of multiple glomeruli, and that postsynaptic calcium increases and glutamate receptor activation are necessary for the neurovascular coupling.
in the olfactory bulb, the relationship between blood flow and neuronal activity is complex and involves several levels of integration.
the local CBF response in the olfactory bulb glomeral layer is driven by the activity of the olfactory nerve terminals, which release glutamate and activate postsynaptic receptors on mitral cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the local CBF increases are not due to a single neuron, but to a population of neurons.
the vascular responses to odor are independent of the activity of single glomeruli.
in the rodent main olfactory bulb, odor-evoked increases in CBF are independent of postsynaptic activity in individual glomeruli.
